## 3. State keyed by tab id

- **`next` counter:** it is now kept in step with the tab count after every close. Opening a tab after a close gives `t(N+1)`, so closing the last tab and then opening a new one reuses that key. This is tested.
- **URL sync:** `toQuery` derives from the renumbered keys, so it stays contiguous with no change needed.
- **Active tab:** this module has no active-tab field. `src/tabs/` is just `tab-keys.mjs` with `{ next, tabs }`, and nothing in the repo calls `closeTab`. I did not add an active field, because that would be a new feature beyond narrow scope. My test only shows a tab remains identifiable by title after renumbering. Any consumer that stores an active key (say `t3`) will now point at the wrong tab or none after a close, and must remap it. `closeTab` could return an old-key to new-key mapping to help, but that changes its return shape, so I left it.

## 4. Commands run

- `npm test` (runs `node --test`): 11 tests, 11 pass, 0 fail. One test failed on the first run because my own expected titles were wrong, and I fixed the test.
- `python3 .claude/hooks/precedent-context.py --self-test`: passing, checked only to confirm the hook still works.

## 5. Unresolved

- **Remounts:** keys are the React key, so the remount cost recorded in the old entry still applies. After a close, every tab to its right gets a new key and loses scroll position and unsaved form input. The UI that consumes these keys is not in this repo, so I couldn't fix it here. I did not hack around it. A clean fix would be a separate stable `id` per tab used as the React key, with `key` kept only for the URL, but that changes the data model and was outside your instruction.
- **Unknown key:** `closeTab` with a key that doesn't exist still re-keys every tab. On an already-contiguous state that changes nothing, which a test confirms.
